lines.japanese: 「あ、昨日の夜は帰りが遅くなってごめんね」
lines.english: “Oh—sorry I came home so late last night.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ……あっ、いえ」
lines.english: “Huh...? Oh. No, it’s fine.”

lines.japanese: 「いつもおいしい夕食をありがとう。豚肉とにんにくの芽を炒めたやつ、おいしかったな」
lines.english: “And thank you for always making such good dinners. The pork and garlic shoots were delicious.”

lines.japanese: 「う、うん……うんっ」
lines.english: “Y-yeah... Yeah!”

lines.japanese: 土曜日の朝食。時間に余裕があるから、心にも余裕があるのかもしれない。話のネタが次から次に生まれてきた。絶好調だ。
lines.english: Saturday breakfast. Perhaps having time to spare left me with room to breathe as well. One topic after another sprang to mind. I was on a roll.

lines.japanese: 「あれってビタミンＢが豊富な料理なんだよね。叔母さんのもおいしいけど、小鳩も上手に作れるようになったよ。あれなら叔母さんが作るのと、そんなに変わらないんじゃないかな」
lines.english: “That dish is full of vitamin B, isn’t it? Auntie makes it well, but you’ve become a wonderful cook too. Yours hardly tastes any different from hers now.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そんなことはあらんです」
lines.english: “Th-that is not so.”

lines.japanese: 「そんな、ほんとにおいしかったんだから、謙遜なんてしなくていいよ。叔母さんたちに作ってあげたらビックリするんじゃないかな」
lines.english: “It really was delicious. There’s no need to be modest. I bet Auntie and Uncle would be amazed if you made it for them.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだ、小鳩の手伝いが出来るように、おれも料理の練習しようかな」
lines.english: “I know. Maybe I should practice cooking too, so I can help you.”

lines.japanese: 「わ、悪いから」
lines.english: “Y-you shouldn’t have to.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなことないよ、小鳩にばかり迷惑をかけられないもの」
lines.english: “Of course I should. I can’t keep burdening you with everything.”

lines.japanese: 「や、やらせるわけにはいかぬ」
lines.english: “I-I cannot permit it.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そうだ。せっかく料理を誉めてるところで悪いんだけど、今日は昼ごはんいらないんだ」
lines.english: “Oh, right. I’m sorry to say this just as I’m praising your cooking, but I won’t need lunch today.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 彼女の黒い瞳が、くりんと大きく見開いた。
lines.english: Her black eyes opened wide and round.

lines.japanese: 「友だ……クラスメイトのところで、学校の作業をしなくちゃいけなくてさ。そっちで適当に何か買って食べるから、今日はいらないんだ」
lines.english: “I have to do some schoolwork at a frien—at a classmate’s house. I’ll buy something to eat while I’m out, so you don’t need to make lunch.”

lines.japanese: 「そうなんだ」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩はこくこくと首を縦に振った。小さな鳩みたいなこの動きはもう見慣れてきた。名は体を表すものなのかな。
lines.english: Kobato bobbed her head several times. By now I was used to the motion, so like a little dove. Perhaps her name really did suit her.

lines.japanese: 「夕飯はどうしますか？」
lines.english: “What will you do about dinner?”

lines.japanese: 「夕飯？　んー、昨日みたいなことになっても悪いしなあ」
lines.english: “Dinner? Hmm. I’d feel bad if the same thing happened as yesterday.”

lines.japanese: 「よし、決めた。遅くなるかもしれないし、自分で食べてくる」
lines.english: “All right, I’ve decided. I may be late, so I’ll eat something while I’m out.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そか。じゃあ、私も吉川さん家で食べてくるから」
lines.english: “I-I see. Then I shall eat at Yoshikawa’s house.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ、小鳩も出かけるんだ」
lines.english: “Oh? You’re going out too, Kobato?”

lines.japanese: 僕が出不精なせいで、叔父さんと叔母さんのいない今の状況だと、小鳩は出かけたくても出かけられなかったのかもしれない。たまには友達と遊んできてね。お兄ちゃんも頑張るよ。
lines.english: Perhaps my own homebody habits had kept Kobato from going out when she wanted while our aunt and uncle were away. Go enjoy yourself with your friend for once. Your big brother would do his best too.

lines.japanese: 「さて、じゃあ準備をしなくちゃいけないから食器は自分で洗っておくね。ごちそうさま」
lines.english: “Well, I have to get ready, so I’ll wash my own dishes. Thank you for breakfast.”

lines.japanese: 僕よりも早く起きて朝食の準備をしてくれた妹と全国の農家の皆さんに向けて手を合わせると、僕は食器を持って立ちあがろうとした。
lines.english: I pressed my palms together in gratitude to my sister, who had risen before me to make breakfast, and to all the farmers of Japan. Then I gathered my dishes and started to stand.

lines.japanese: 「あ、まま、待って」
lines.english: “Ah—w-wait.”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 僕は中腰のまま、引きとめて妹の顔を見た。今まで彼女の方から僕に声をかけることなんて、数えるくらいしかなかったのに。
lines.english: Halfway to my feet, I stopped and looked at my sister. Until now, I could count on one hand the times she had spoken to me first.

lines.japanese: 「その、お友達は学校の、ひと、ひと？」
lines.english: “That friend... Are they from your school? A p-person from school?”

lines.japanese: 「え？　うん、そうだよ。なんで？」
lines.english: “Yes. Why?”

lines.japanese: 「こないだ、電話くれたひと？」
lines.english: “The person who called the other day?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 電話くれたひと……まあ、というよりも、僕宛てに電話してくるひとなんて、一人しかいない。
lines.english: The person who called... Or rather, there was only one person who ever called asking for me.

lines.japanese: 今日、このあと会うのは小鳩の言う通り渡来さんで……でも、なんだろう。なんとなくはっきりとは言いづらかった。
lines.english: Just as Kobato suspected, I was going to see Watarai today. But somehow, I found it difficult to say so plainly.

lines.japanese: だけど、隠すことでもないし……家族に出かける先を伝えておくのは当然のことだ。
lines.english: Still, it was nothing to hide. It was only natural to tell one’s family where one was going.

lines.japanese: 「うん、あのひと……渡来さんって言うんだ」
lines.english: “Yes. That person... her name is Watarai.”

lines.japanese: 「わたらいさん」
lines.english: “Watarai.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩は一度こくんと大きく、そのあとこくりと小さくうなずいた。
lines.english: Kobato gave one large bob of the head, then a smaller nod.

lines.japanese: 「えと、さっきから楽しそう？」
lines.english: “Um... You’ve seemed happy all morning?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 楽しそう？　小鳩にそんなことを言われるとは思わなかった。今の僕って楽しそうに見えるのかな。
lines.english: Happy? I had not expected to hear that from Kobato. Did I really look happy?

lines.japanese: 「え、別に普通だよ。なにがいつもと違うの」
lines.english: “I-I’m perfectly normal. What’s different about me?”

lines.japanese: 「んっ……うん、なんとなく」
lines.english: “Mm... I don’t know. Just something.”

lines.japanese: 「な、なんとなくじゃないよ」
lines.english: “‘Just something’ isn’t an answer.”

lines.japanese: 僕は小鳩に対して抗議をしようとしたが、残念ながら彼女がこくこくとうなずいてしまったため、抗議自体が不発に終わった。
lines.english: I tried to lodge a protest, but unfortunately Kobato began bobbing her head, and my protest died before it could begin.

lines.japanese: 「うん……うん」
lines.english: “Yes... yes.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩は手元を見つめながら、幾度かうなずいている。
lines.english: Kobato kept her gaze on her hands and nodded several more times.

lines.japanese: 「あ、じゃあ……今度こそ、食器を洗いに行ってくるよ」
lines.english: “Well, then... This time I really am going to wash the dishes.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、ありがとう」
lines.english: “Okay. Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩は僕よりも食べるのが遅かったから、小さいお茶碗に入ったごはんをもくもくと食べはじめた。僕は体を立ちあがらせると、食器を持って居間を出る。
lines.english: Kobato ate more slowly than I did. She returned in silence to the rice in her little bowl. I rose, gathered my dishes, and left the living room.

lines.japanese: 「……がんばってね」
lines.english: “...Do your best.”

lines.japanese: 襖を跨ごうとしたとき、後ろから小さくそんな声が聞こえた。だけどあまりに小さい声だったから、それが聞き間違いなのか自信が持てない僕は、何も言わずに台所へと向かった。
lines.english: As I stepped across the threshold, I heard that tiny voice behind me. It was so faint that I could not be certain I had heard correctly, so I went to the kitchen without answering.

lines.japanese: 食器を洗いながら時間を見ると、時計の針は９時ちょうどに近い位置を指していた。髪をセットして服を選ぶには、まだまだ充分に余裕があった。
lines.english: While washing the dishes, I checked the time. The hands were nearing nine. I still had more than enough time to style my hair and choose what to wear.
